title: Prove charge-only ternary guard costs through two additions (no κ)
body:
## Summary

For full affine ternary guard families, hidden dual data at zero image coordinates cannot change the optimal monomial-header cost through two row additions.

```text
multiset of scalar/vector charges -> min(optimal paid-addition cost, 3)
```

Claim type: scoped written mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration. The theorem holds in every dimension and for multiple slope rows. Any equal-charge pair with different prices must have smaller price at least three. This is a new partial answer to Open next question 1 of SHIN09-git's [#6712](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6712), pinned at `03caa7f6cb5bd21c834024e9d81f6b43eb325b91`.

The new step replaces any successful two-addition word touching a zero-charge coordinate by a charge-visible word. It builds on the credited separation, component-charge and scalar-settlement lemmas. No predecessor executable, receipt or full census is replayed. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

Only `research/ternary-two-addition-charge-invariance/` is added. The selected frontier is unchanged. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19440678).

## Evidence

Before, charge sufficiency in the unanchored ternary model was open. The new all-dimension proof resolves the zero-, one- and two-addition sublevels.

CPython 3.12.15, standard library only: both direct modes and the registered package pass. The verifier checks 1,256 orbit representatives, 221 dimension-tagged charge fibers, 46 local scalar cases, 2,916 dense header actions and 19 literal two-coordinate guard families. Three semantic corruptions are rejected. Cost three in the finite output means at least three, since expansion stops after two levels.

Each registered command took under 0.1 seconds locally. The complete registered launcher took 0.417 seconds. The committed-byte/source-history preflight passes at `3ae29191befb4289cf4a187f685bce8d4f129cf8`. Both standalone modes also pass from committed Git-archive bytes with an empty PATH and no Git metadata; their complete generated receipts match local output.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/ternary-two-addition-charge-invariance/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/ternary-two-addition-charge-invariance/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/ternary-two-addition-charge-invariance
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/ternary-two-addition-charge-invariance --check-source-history
```

The standalone output is `PASS_TERNARY_TWO_ADDITION_CHARGE_INVARIANCE`, with zero failed checks and proof/verifier SHA256 hashes. Other hosts may substitute their CPython 3.12 path.

## Limitations

Full affine families over F3 only, with free permutations and nonzero scalings, unit-priced additions and no added coordinates. This is a written universal proof; finite corroboration uses one slope row. Higher prices, partial families, other fields, physical delivery/restoration, complete recursive invoices and supplier admission are unproved here. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. All five selected framework assumptions remain; no new kappa or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. Lean, Docker and unrelated historical suites were not run.

## Open next questions

Does charge sufficiency hold at costs at least three? Start with a three-addition component containing two opposite slope charges and two initially zero-charge coordinates. Four vertices can retain three nonzero scalar charges, so the present one-settlement replacement argument does not apply. This is a proposed next step, not a claimed counterexample at three additions.

## Related open work

- [#6712](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6712): direct predecessor and source of the open question; its general settlement and scalar-price results are credited inputs, while this supplies a new bounded charge-sufficiency theorem.
- [#6753](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6753): reviews the predecessor's anchored settlement implication; this is an original unanchored sublevel theorem rather than another review.
- [#6710](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6710): studies the same common-image guards under uniform full-GL headers; this uses a paid monomial-header metric.
- [#6748](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6748): reviews that full-GL counting law; no count or review is repeated here.
- [#6701](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6701): treats independent binary common-image guard probabilities, a different field/header measure from this ternary operation-cost result.
- [#6703](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6703): treats transpose-dual all-field common-covector pair correlation; this proves a truncated paid distance for complete affine families.

The final own-open-PR check found no additional related work among this account's PRs created since the claim.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks, `plan` and `replay (research/ternary-two-addition-charge-invariance)`, passed for commit `3ae29191befb4289cf4a187f685bce8d4f129cf8` in [run 42223987205](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42223987205). All declared normal and optimized checks also passed locally. CI success is finite replay evidence, not independent mathematical or proof-kernel acceptance.

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: package. The change adds an isolated proof and opt-in verifier; it changes no shared code or selected result.
